originalReceipt.text: job-wide private commit including descendants; different from sampled private working set or whole application limit

correction.correctTerm: sampled sum of per-process private committed bytes (PrivateUsage), across all live acceptance-Job members
correction.replacementScope: Windows Job committed-memory protection for the owned bridge process and its contained descendants only. Acceptance separately samples the sum of per-process PrivateUsage private committed bytes for all live members of the whole-application acceptance Job at nominal1-second intervals. These differ in scope and enforcement/observation timing; the acceptance privateBytes field is not working set, and the bridge budget is not a whole-application limit.

codeLines: 1058-1080: completion-port messages and queried limit-violation evidence
bridgeRuntimeProtection.metric: Kernel Job committed virtual-memory accounting/limit for the bridge-owned Job membership; no process working-set counter is used to set these limits.
bridgeRuntimeProtection.scope: The self-created bridge Job and its contained bridge descendants; not Token Meow main process or all WebViews. Exact membership/creation and containment evidence belongs to the existing owned tests and future native receipts.
bridgeRuntimeProtection.timing: Hard Job limit participates in commit allocation enforcement. Warning is a kernel notification threshold observed asynchronously by the bridge monitor, then handled by the application; it is not a sampled private-memory peak and notification does not itself impose the hard stop.
bridgeRuntimeProtection.limits: An allocation denied by the configured hard cap or a warning does not prove the complete application meets350/600MiB. Preserve the original receipt limits on notification evidence and possible ordinary EOF/timeout classification.

codeLines: 84-93: Job CPU accounting and separate kernel peak field
94-126: enumerate original Job members, open handle, validate creation, read memory and sum
121-125: PrivateUsage -> privateBytes and WorkingSetSize -> workingSetBytes separately
currentWholeApplicationAcceptance.privateBytes: Sum of each currently enumerated live member PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX.PrivateUsage. PrivateUsage is private committed memory/commit charge, not resident working-set pages.
currentWholeApplicationAcceptance.workingSetBytes: A separate sum from WorkingSetSize. The observer does not label this privateBytes and the600MiB check does not use it.
currentWholeApplicationAcceptance.scope: Outer acceptance Job rooted in the exact launched Token Meow application, including its live WebView and bridge descendants; observer/helper outside the Job.
currentWholeApplicationAcceptance.timing: Nominal1-second samples enumerate/read member processes sequentially, not one atomic instant. The reported sampled private peak is max(sample.privateBytes) across the original interval. Short-lived or inter-sample peaks may not appear; sample gaps and membership errors are separately gated.

thresholdSource.lines: 118-123: no measurement errors, gap<=2.5s, sample.privateBytes>600MB -> threshold failure

currentWholeApplicationAcceptance.kernelPeakSeparate: jobLifetimePeakCommitBytes is populated from QueryInformationJobObject ExtendedLimit.PeakJobMemoryUsed at resource-job.cs90-93. It is a kernel-maintained Job peak counter and stays separate from the maximum of sampled process PrivateUsage sums; it cannot be relabelled as sampled working set or silently substituted into the existing acceptance gate.

legacyProcessObserver.line: 86: PrivateMemorySize64 and WorkingSet64 are separately read into private/working variables.
legacyProcessObserver.meaning: This older observer also distinguishes private byte size from working set. Its process-discovery/coverage limitations and any old receipts remain unchanged; it is not promoted to the current Job protocol.

authoritativeReferences.supports: PrivateUsage represents process private committed memory/commit charge; WorkingSetSize is a separate member.
JobMemoryLimit with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_JOB_MEMORY controls committed virtual memory for the Job; kernel peak tracking is separate from sample aggregation.
JobMemoryLimit is a Job-wide committed-memory notification threshold; notification permits continued allocation and requires monitor-side handling.

comparisonBoundaries: Do not contrast committed Job protection against a purported sampled private working set: the actual acceptance field is private committed bytes.

Both are commit-related concepts, but the protected bridge subgroup, outer acceptance membership, sequential sampling, kernel enforcement and lifetime-peak observation are different scopes/times. Their numbers are not interchangeable and no equality is assumed.
No350/600MiB threshold, original failure, sample gap, original counter, candidate, build receipt or old targeted receipt is changed.
This is a terminology/measurement clarification only; no test, runtime resource, release or M4 qualification is added.
